title: Exposure-oriented machine learning prioritizes nobiletin as a colorectal cancer candidate
summary: Four machine-learning models gave a composite score to 47 exposure-related parent compounds profiled by serum UPLC-QTOF-MS/MS, and nobiletin ranked first (score 0.77). Nobiletin inhibited CT26 proliferation (24-h IC50 70.8 uM) and suppressed tumour growth in syngeneic CT26 mice without body-weight loss. Abstract only; model names, ablation and mouse numbers were not read, and only the top-ranked compound was tested.
ai_technology: Four machine-learning models producing a composite prioritization score
organization: Nanjing University of Chinese Medicine; Suzhou Traditional Chinese Medicine Hospital

evidence.tested: In vitro proliferation and EdU assays and a syngeneic CT26 mouse tumour model.
evidence.unknown: Model names, mouse numbers; activity of lower-ranked compounds; full text not reviewed.
